sentences.text: On the newest quarter the premise holds as revenue: year-on-year growth sped up from the prior quarter, and Data Center supplied nearly all of that growth, so the company-wide acceleration is in substance a Data Center acceleration.

The fiscal-year basis tells the opposite story: Data Center growth slowed by 74.2 percentage points in fiscal 2026, so 'still' is true only if the newest quarters, not the last full year, are the right frame.

The record measures shipped revenue, not demand, and the filing itself says production complexity has caused supply and demand challenges and revenue volatility, so revenue could understate or lag demand in either direction.

Billings ahead of delivery grew faster than revenue, which leans toward demand outrunning shipments, while receivables also grew faster than revenue, which means part of the booked growth has not yet turned into cash.

For a purchase decision the step from acceleration to value is that the 2026-09-30 price needs 13.4% a year for 10 years, far below current growth, but that arithmetic leans most on holding a 65.2% operating margin; at the industry's 90th-percentile margin it needs 28.1% a year, and no peer of this size in the record sustained even the base rate.
The CEO's resignation was filed after the newest 10-Q and after the price date, so nothing in this record shows whether demand or the valuation absorbed it.
Data Center grew +116.6% in the latest quarter against +68.2% for fiscal 2026, so the quarterly pace is well above the annual one that showed slowing.
Revenue rose in each of the 8 quarters while growth on a larger base still accelerated, and the company's growth rank among SIC 3674 filers stayed near the top.
Deferred revenue up +215.1% against revenue up +105.9% is the closest proxy in the record to demand ahead of delivery, and it points the same way.
The only Data Center pace comparison the record computes is annual, and it shows slowing; the quarterly Data Center acceleration is inferred from the company total rather than measured directly.
Receivable days rose from 54.1 to 59.6, so some of the accelerating revenue is booked but uncollected, which weakens reading it as pure end demand.
The filing names supply constraints as a source of revenue volatility, so a quarter's acceleration could reflect timing of production rather than a change in demand.
Whether the quarterly acceleration persists in the next 10-Q, rather than the annual slowdown reasserting itself.
Whether deferred revenue keeps growing faster than revenue, the record's best stand-in for demand not yet shipped.
Whether the 65.2% operating margin the price leans on holds, since acceleration matters to the decision only through that margin.

conditions.text: Quarterly revenue falling below the Q2 FY2027 level would break the 8-quarter rise and undercut acceleration.
Deferred revenue falling below its Q2 FY2027 level would remove the main proxy for demand ahead of shipments.
A results 8-K reporting slowing Data Center growth would test the claim before the next 10-Q.
